To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the psychiatric charts of the women and men we analyzed were filled with gender normativity, heterosexism and homophobia, and that these were conflated in a way that was not true of the men's charts.
psychiatrists implicitly construed troubled female-male relationships and sexual encounters, as well as nonconformity to gender role expectations, as indices of psychopathy.

1) The heteronormal is implicitly conflated with the psychiatric normal in physician dictated psychiatric charts, 2) This heteronormal/psychiatric normal conflation was used to pathologize women and men who did not conform to gendered expectations of heteronormality and 3) The heteronormative/psychiatric normal conflations were deployed to pathologize same sex relationships and same sex sexual encounters.
In summary, our research is concerned with

how gender role conformity is implicated in psychiatric determinations of sanity and how the heterosexualizing of psychiatric normality has functioned as a means of regulating gender and sexual non conformity.
the ways in which gender role conformity and heteronormativity are conflated in the diagnosis of mental illness and how this process contributes to the heterosexualization of sanity.
how gender and sexuality are constructed in psychiatric diagnosis and treatment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
heterosexism is a form of oppression that is embedded within our culture and that it is not limited to the LGBT community.
heteronormativity and homophobia are the two major reasons why homosexuality is still not fully accepted in the society.

the heterosexualization of sanity and the psychiatric normalizing of heterosexuality are not simply a matter of psychiatric diagnosis, but a cultural process that is embedded in a larger social context.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

heteronormative expectations of female and male gender roles and sexual behavior, which are not only prevalent in U.S. culture but are also embedded in psychiatric diagnostic categories, are used by physicians to diagnose mental health problems.
the heteronormativity of sanity is not a matter of explicit heterosexism but of implicit heteronormativity.

the heteronormative psychiatric normal was not only an ideological tool for the medicalization of women's and men' mental health, but it was also a powerful mechanism for the heterosexualization of sanity in the U.S.
The main takeaway from our work is that
heterosexism, like homophobia, is not simply a personal attitude, but a social system that is embedded in the institutions and structures of society.
gender and sexuality are conflations of mental health and illness.

the depathologizing of homosexuality from the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders (DSM) in 1973 did not end the pathologizing of homosexuality, rather, it was replaced by a more subtle and implicit heterosexualizing of sanity.
